A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Mind the Gap, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–F. All appendix pages are identical between versions, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on GSM8K, MATH, Natural Question, and Sudoku, including verification comparisons, scaling analyses, and iterative self-improvement results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–6 and Appendices B–C, including benchmark tables, ablations, and verification analyses.

M1.justification: The generation–verification–update framework, rejection sampling and RL updates, verification mechanisms, and ensemble procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the method details in Appendices A and D are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GSM8K, MATH, Natural Question, and 4-by-4 Sudoku coverage. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The MC, CoT-Binary, CoT-Score, Tournament, ensemble, and fixed-verifier comparisons retain the same participants. The newly cited studies in Section 7 are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain unchanged, including 128 responses per prompt, one verification per response, sampling parameters, model configurations, thresholds, and metrics. Figure 4's revised RL wording does not introduce another experimental setting.

E4.justification: The temperature, instruct-model, fixed-verifier, and verifier-variance ablations in Appendix B are identical. Threshold sensitivity, correlation analyses, diversity analyses, and ensemble experiments also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same distribution means and standard deviations and Appendix B.4 verifier-variance analysis. There are no changes to seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains Qwen-2-72B Sudoku accuracy of 8.82% and a gap of 16.99 percentage points.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.2, the reweighting formulation, the improvement bound in Section 2, and the formal verification descriptions in Appendix A are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning GV-Gap, scaling, task-dependent self-improvement, iterative saturation, and verification ensembles.

C2.justification: Explanations of formatting-related accuracy gains, verification behavior, and declining diversity are retained. The observational-scaling qualification, task limitations, and proposed future directions are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation information remains identical, including Table 9's training hyperparameters, Appendix E's prompts, and Appendix F's A100 infrastructure description. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds Chen et al. (2024) on self-play fine-tuning, Jiang et al. (2024) on self-refinement, and Damani et al. (2024) on adaptive inference computation. These are limited citation additions without substantive repositioning. Anonymous (2024) becomes Huang et al. (2025), but the matching title and reference identify the same sharpening-mechanism work.

P1.justification: Localized edits adjust capitalization, punctuation, caption wording, and bibliographic attribution. The section order, explanations, and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: There are small spacing changes around Figure 1, positioning adjustments within Figure 3, and reference-page reflow. Figure 4's caption changes '7B-RL' to 'RL'; its plot is unchanged. No figures or tables are added or removed, and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: Section 7 modestly broadens acknowledgment of relevant self-improvement and inference-computation research, while the previously anonymous theoretical reference receives full attribution. Together with small editorial corrections, this improves scholarly completeness slightly; the scientific evidence, analysis, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
